messages.subject: Equivalence of nested.update function in geomorph 3.1
parts:
Hello Morphometricians,

I was updating the code of a previous project to the new version of geomorph, and am having difficulty in replicating an analysis with the nested.update() function. I have consulted the online vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/geomorph/vignettes/geomorph.assistance.html), which has solved most of my updates except this one. I was hoping someone could indicate me the equivalent code in the new geomorph version for the code I give below. With that it should suffice to tweak out my other functions or create them anew. Hopefully this equivalence also helps out other users.

For context, I have three species divided into three age categories. The code for geomorph v3.0.7 in R v3.5.1 that I want to replicate is the following:

## age and species are factors with three levels
gdfAllo <- geomorph.data.frame(Y.gpa,species=spp,age=age)
allometry <- procD.lm(coords ~log(Csize)*species + species/age,data=gdfAllo,iter=9999)
allometry <- nested.update(allometry, ~species/age)
summary(allometry)
x11();plot(allometry, type = "regression",
           predictor = log(gdfAllo$Csize),
           reg.type = "PredLine",
           pch = 21,
           bg = as.numeric(gdfAllo$species),
           xlab = "lnCS")

Thanks in advance.


Best regards,
Javier

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: Equivalence of nested.update function in geomorph 3.1
parts:
Javier,

 

The nested.updates() components are now available in lm.rrpp in the RRPP package, which performs the analytics for procD.lm now.

 

In particular, there is the option for ‘error=’ where one specifies various error terms. The tutorial that accompanies RRPP provides an example.

Dean

parts:
Hi Dean and Mike,

Thanks for the fast reply! I was also rather fast in comparing my script between versions and overlooked more important details... The nested.update() function works as before, but now with the error argument in the anova function (as in the example of the vignette).

The incongruence between versions that I am obtaining is in the results of the formula:

Call:  #old version
procD.lm(f1 = coords ~log(Csize)*species + species/age, data=gdfAllo, iter=999)
Call:  #new version
procD.lm(coords ~log(Csize)*species + species/age, data=gdfAllo,iter=999)

What appears to be the same analysis gives different anova z-scores and p-values in the different versions of geomorph that I am running. What really confuses me though is that the plots for this analysis (using the same code from my previous email) are also different between versions. [I am attaching the plots and anova tables for both versions in the attachment.] The difference is notable, but I can't figure out why it occurs. Is there a difference in how procD.lm() handles its arguments in the newer version of geomorph? Is there a differenec within the plotting code I'm using? or Where could this incongruence come from? Thanks again in advance.


Best wishes,
Javier

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Equivalence of nested.update function in geomorph 3.1
parts:
Javier,

For your plots, one appears to have an interaction term and one doesn’t.

For your ANOVA differences, you have asked us what could be different between versions that are 6 updates and over 17 months apart.  This is too severe of a request for us to to do the fishing for you.  I recommend you look at the various updates that were logged on our NEWS file: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/geomorph/news/news.html for geomorph, or https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RRPP/news/news.html for RRPP (affects geomorph for versions 3.1.0 and higher).  Look at bug fixes.  Alternatively, you can go back to maybe version 3.1.6 and get ANOVA tables for that version and every subsequent version, so you can isolate when the change happened.  That way we can identify, e.g., between version 3.0.x and 3.0.y which changes were made.  To answer your question more broadly, there are many possible reasons for the incongruence.  If this is a change from the last version, I could probably give you a more precise reason or seek a solution if there was a bug in the code.

Judging by the values, the old code had a bug because there is no way an F value of 1.3445 (small) should induce a Z-score of 4.8826 (huge!).  If I remember correctly — and this has happened often — upon release of the geomorph upgrade on CRAN, a bug was detected, and we probably fixed it on github.  Since the following version, 3.1.0, was  major upgrade and included depending procD.lm on RRPP, the history of fixes on github might be a little lost between those two versions.

I think you had an older version that had required a bug fix that you did not install and this is the reason for the disparate results.  But as that was 6 versions ago, it is only a guess.

Mike

allometry <- nested.update(allometry, ~species/age)
summary(allometry)
x11();plot(allometry, type = "regression",
           predictor = log(gdfAllo$Csize),
           reg.type = "PredLine",
           pch = 21,
           bg = as.numeric(gdfAllo$species),
           xlab = "lnCS")
 
Thanks in advance.
